mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand, which positively impacts the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of rising HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in FEDFUNDS below 3% signals monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow when FEDFUNDS drops below 3%.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) alongside high FEDFUNDS indicates a tightening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur when UNRATE is low and FEDFUNDS are high.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow increased INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow rising PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) with low FEDFUNDS boosts demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not occur with rising RSAFS and low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 3% may lead to Fed tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not follow when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: Slow GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not occur when GDPC1 growth is slow.
